nodes.description: State variable holding the reference to the BIT (8thereum) token contract used for external token transfers and balance queries.
State variable storing the contract owner address, set to msg.sender in the constructor and used by onlyOwner.
Boolean state variable gating gameplay through the isOpenToPublic modifier, set true by openToThePublic.
State variable holding the pseudo-randomly generated winning number derived from keccak256, blockhash and msg.sender, modulo 5, plus 1.
Mapping of player address to the amount of tokens accounted as already paid into the game.
Constructor that initializes BITcontract, sets openToPublic to false and assigns owner = msg.sender.
Public payable-game entry point guarded by isOpenToPublic and onlyRealPeople; computes a pseudo-random winning number and pays half the contract balance to the winner.
Public view helper returning BITcontract.balanceOf(someAddress).
Public view helper returning BITcontract.gamePlayers(address(this), customerAddress).
Public view returning half of the contract's BIT balance.
Public view returning the BIT balance of a hard-coded whale address.
Owner-only function that flips openToPublic to true, allowing players to interact.
Owner-only rescue function that transfers arbitrary ERC20 tokens held by the contract, with a notBIT guard.
Attacker-controllable caller address used for ownership, player accounting, randomness and payout destination.
Transaction origin used in the onlyRealPeople check, enabling phishing-style bypass through an intermediary contract.
External call BITcontract.transfer(msg.sender, tokensToWinner) performed inside start before state is fully finalized, enabling reentrancy via the token contract.
External call ERC20Interface(tokenAddress).transfer(tokenOwner, tokens) on an arbitrary, attacker-influenced token contract.
Access-control require(msg.sender == owner) enforced by the onlyOwner modifier.
require(msg.sender == tx.origin) enforced by onlyRealPeople; native-tx assumption that gives no real anti-bot/anti-contract guarantee.
Weak randomness source: uint256(keccak256(blockhash(block.number-1), choice, msg.sender)) can be predicted/manipulated by miners or by the caller.
Arithmetic expression '%5 + 1' applied to the randomness hash to derive winningNumber.
Arithmetic expression 'balance / 2' used to compute the winner payout and winners pot.
User-supplied number chosen by the player in start, fed into the randomness hash and compared with winningNumber.
Address argument of BITBalanceOf whose BIT balance is queried.
Customer address argument of getTokensPaidToGame used to query gamePlayers.
Arbitrary ERC20 token contract address supplied to returnAnyERC20Token and used as external call target.
Destination address supplied by the owner to returnAnyERC20Token.
Token amount supplied by the owner to returnAnyERC20Token.
Local flag in start indicating whether the player matched the winning number.
Local value in start holding the tokens paid to the game by the caller, compared against paidPlayers.
Local value in start holding half of the contract's BIT balance to be paid to the winner.
Local value in winnersPot holding the contract's BIT balance before halving.

edges.reason: msg.sender is written into the owner state variable in the constructor, granting privileged rights to the deployer.
owner is compared against msg.sender in the onlyOwner require check.
onlyOwner restricts openToThePublic to the owner.
onlyOwner restricts the ERC20 rescue function returnAnyERC20Token to the owner.
openToThePublic writes true into the openToPublic state variable.
isOpenToPublic modifier requires openToPublic to be true before start can execute.
msg.sender is compared with tx.origin in the onlyRealPeople require check.
tx.origin is compared with msg.sender in the onlyRealPeople require check.
onlyRealPeople gates execution of start based on the tx.origin equality check.
The player-chosen value choice is an input to the keccak256 randomness computation.
msg.sender is an input to the keccak256 randomness computation, making the outcome caller-influenced.
The keccak256 hash result is reduced modulo 5 and incremented by 1 to form the winning number.
The modulo arithmetic result is stored into the winningNumber state variable.
winningNumber is compared with choice to decide whether the player wins and a payout occurs.
The tokensTransferred local is compared with and written back into paidPlayers[msg.sender].
start calls getTokensPaidToGame(msg.sender) to obtain the tokens paid by the caller.
The return value of getTokensPaidToGame is assigned to the tokensTransferred local variable.
start calls BITBalanceOf(address(this)) to size the payout.
The BITcontract state variable provides the external contract used for the transfer call.
The tokensToWinner local value is passed as the amount to BITcontract.transfer.
msg.sender is used as the recipient of the external transfer in start.
start executes the external BITcontract.transfer before returning, leaving mid-function external control flow.
The external BIT token transfer can call back into start, enabling reentrancy against the paidPlayers/balance accounting.
returnAnyERC20Token performs an external call on a caller-supplied token contract.
tokenAddress is used as the target contract of the external ERC20 transfer.
tokenOwner is used as the destination address of the external ERC20 transfer.
tokens is used as the amount of the external ERC20 transfer.
An arbitrary ERC20 contract supplied by the owner can call back into the calling contract during transfer.
winnersPot calls BITBalanceOf(this) to read the contract's BIT balance.
The balance local in winnersPot is divided by 2.
The halved balance produced by the arithmetic operation is returned by winnersPot.
BITWhaleBalance calls BITBalanceOf on the hard-coded whale address.
choice is declared as the parameter of start.
someAddress is declared as the parameter of BITBalanceOf.
customerAddress is declared as the parameter of getTokensPaidToGame.
tokenAddress is declared as the parameter of returnAnyERC20Token.
tokenOwner is declared as the parameter of returnAnyERC20Token.
tokens is declared as the parameter of returnAnyERC20Token.
didYouWin is a local variable declared in start and returned to the caller.
tokensTransferred is a local variable declared in start.
tokensToWinner is a local variable declared in start.
balance is a local variable declared in winnersPot.

normalization_plan.reason: choice is only meaningful as the player input parameter of start, so it is normalized into the start function node.
someAddress is only used as the balance-query parameter of BITBalanceOf and is normalized into that function.
customerAddress is only used as the lookup parameter of getTokensPaidToGame and is normalized into that function.
tokenAddress exists only as the target-token parameter of returnAnyERC20Token and is normalized into that function.
tokenOwner exists only as the recipient parameter of returnAnyERC20Token and is normalized into that function.
tokens exists only as the amount parameter of returnAnyERC20Token and is normalized into that function.
didYouWin is a transient flag inside start and is normalized into the start function node.
tokensTransferred is a transient local inside start used for payment bookkeeping and is normalized into the start function node.
tokensToWinner is consumed directly by the external BITcontract.transfer call and is normalized into that unsafe operation node.
balance is only used by the balance/2 arithmetic expression and is normalized into that arithmetic operation node.
